title: Overdue Hosting Renewals at Checkout — Web Hosting Plans
content:
## Web Hosting Plans — renewing a plan whose term end date has come

**Scope.** This pricing governs a renewal that the account holder pays at Harborline's checkout for a plan whose term end date is on or before today and which carries no scheduled downgrade request, and only such a renewal. A renewal that the account holder pays at Harborline's checkout for a plan whose term end date is later than today and which carries no scheduled downgrade or term change request is priced by Harborline's early renewal pricing. Every other renewal — an auto-renew charge, a renewal that applies a scheduled downgrade request, or a renewal paid at checkout while the term end date is later than today for a plan with a scheduled term change request — is billed at the regular rate of the tier and term length that the new term will have (the regular 12, 24 or 36-month rate multiplied by the months, or the 1-month price for a 1-month term, with no setup fee), less the account tier's hosting discount percentage, rounded half up to the cent.

**Who pays.** The overdue renewal is the account holder's own payment, completed at Harborline's checkout by card or through PayPal after the agent quotes the amount, because Harborline support never takes payment details; a payment from account credit is not taken under this rule.

**Conditions and effect.** A renewal may be charged only while the plan status is active or suspended. The new term always starts on the previous term end date, even when the renewal is paid late.

### Checkout tool: `bill_overdue_hosting_renewal_c53aa4e7`

The agent unlocks this customer-side tool and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it to complete the payment. It records the payment on the plan's billing history as a manual renewal line covering the new term. The next term begins on the day the previous term ended and runs for the stated number of months: the plan's current term dates move to the new term, its billing term becomes the stated length and the introductory-term flag is cleared. When a scheduled term change request is named, that request is marked as applied.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `hosting_id` | Reference number of the customer's hosting plan being renewed, as given to the customer by the agent from the hosting plan lookup. |
| `amount` | Renewal amount paid, USD, positive, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent. |
| `term_months` | Length of the new term in calendar months: an integer that is one of the offered terms 1, 12, 24 or 36. |
| `payment_method` | How the customer pays: `card` (charged to the customer's payment card) or `paypal` (paid through the customer's PayPal account). |
| `hosting_request_id` | Reference number of the plan's scheduled term change request taken up by this renewal, from the change request lookup; an empty string when the plan has no scheduled term change request. |

**Return.** On success: status "renewed", `hosting_charge_id` (the new renewal line), `order_ref` (Harborline order number, HL- followed by 8 digits), `amount`, `term_months`, `term_start_date` and `term_end_date` (the new term dates), `payment_method` and `hosting_request_id` (the request marked applied, or an empty string). The customer sees the new renewal line with its own order number and the plan's new term end date.

**Errors.** The tool refuses a payment method other than card or PayPal, a term other than 1, 12, 24 or 36 months, an unknown plan, an amount that is not positive, and a named request that is not a scheduled term change request of that plan.
